These restrictions will undermine the ability of companies headquartered in countries of concern from using U.S. advanced Super Intelligence (SI) semiconductors to train advanced SI models. Data centers, foreign foundries, and chip exporters are required to perform robust due diligence on their customers, including any direct or indirect ownership or control by persons in Country Group D:5 or Macau, as part of complying with this new control. The license requirement will not apply to commercial recommender systems, such as those used by online retailers or social media companies, as these functions do not pose the same national security threat. Second, in addition to the current license requirements for advanced semiconductors, a license will be required to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil (and any additional country designated by the Secretary of Commerce, in consultation with the Secretary of State or the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs)--countries which present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion. The license requirement for these five countries will not apply to semiconductors destined to companies headquartered in, or whose ultimate parent company is headquartered in, the United States, provided certain reporting requirements are met. Commerce will be actively monitoring for countries that tolerate evasion of this IFR and will consider a range of consequences for such countries, such as import restrictions, new license requirements on advanced semiconductor exports, downgrading the country's status in the U.S. export control regime, and Entity List designations and temporary export prohibitions for foreign persons involved in such activities. November 16, 2026 at 09:40 AM UTC • By FilingReader AI
China Oilfield Services Limited has signed a contract to commission 59 oilfield support vessels for a total fixed lump-sum price of RMB10,928 million including tax. The order comprises 46 liquefied natural gas-powered platform supply vessels and 13 high-horsepower conventional-powered anchor handling tug supply vessels.

© NickEyes / Adobe Stock
China Oilfield Services Limited (COSL) has signed contracts worth $1.64 billion (RMB10.93 billion) for the construction of 59 offshore support vessels (OSVs), with deliveries scheduled between 2028 and 2030.
The contracts, signed on November 14, cover 46 LNG-powered platform supply vessels (PSVs) and 13 high-horsepower, conventionally powered anchor handling tug supply (AHTS) vessels across six types.
The construction work has been awarded to a consortium led by Fujian Southeast Shipbuilding, alongside Fujian Mawei Shipbuilding and Fujian Funing Shipbuilding Heavy Industry, according to the company's stock exchange announcement dated November 16.
The vessels will primarily operate in China's coastal waters, supporting offshore oil and gas exploration and development, mobile offshore facilities and marine engineering structures.
